title: Localization of the base of a naive cotangent complex
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $S\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative subset (containing $1$ and closed under multiplication), and let $S^{-1}A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings; $B$ is an $A$-algebra by composition. Ring localization is that of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For a ring map $R\to B$, let $C_{B/R}$ be its standard naive cotangent complex [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], written in cohomological degrees $-1,0$: with $P_R=R[x_b\mid b\in B]$ and $I_R=\ker(P_R\to B)$, it is $[I_R/I_R^2\xrightarrow{[h]\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dh}B\otimes_{P_R}\Omega_{P_R/R}]$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The coefficient localization map $A[B]\to(S^{-1}A)[B]$, $x_b\mapsto x_b$, induces the canonical $B$-linear chain map
$$C_{B/A}\longrightarrow C_{B/S^{-1}A}.$$
Its image is an isomorphism in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; in fact this chain map is a homotopy equivalence, meaning that it admits a chain map inverse whose composites differ from the respective identities by maps $dh+hd$, with $h$ of degree $-1$. No injectivity, finite generation, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed; $0\in S$ is allowed whenever the displayed map to $B$ exists.

source.place: Tag 07BS (lemma-NL-localize-bottom), including its canonical map; section-netherlander for the standard presentations.

proof.text: Put $A_S=S^{-1}A$, $P=A[x_b\mid b\in B]$, $P_S=A_S[x_b\mid b\in B]$, and let $T\subseteq P$ be the image of $S$ as constant polynomials. The coefficient map identifies $P_S$ with $T^{-1}P$: a polynomial with finitely many coefficients in $A_S$ has a common denominator $s\in S$, so is $p/s$; if $p/1=0$, each of its finitely many coefficients is annihilated by an element of $S$, and the product of these elements annihilates $p$. The fraction map $p/s\mapsto s^{-1}p$ and the coefficientwise map back are inverse ring maps, fixing all variables. Write $\epsilon:P\to B$ for evaluation and $s_B$ for the image of $s\in S$ in $B$. Each $s_B$ is a unit, since $A\to B$ factors through $A_S$; hence evaluation on $P_S$ is $\epsilon_S(p/s)=s_B^{-1}\epsilon(p)$.

source.place: Tag 07BS (lemma-NL-localize-bottom), localized polynomial presentation; fraction construction in Section 00CM (section-localization).

proof.text: Let $I=\ker\epsilon$ and $J=\ker\epsilon_S$. The evaluation maps are surjective because the variable $x_b$ maps to $b$. For a fraction $p/s\in P_S$, invertibility of $s_B$ gives $\epsilon_S(p/s)=0$ if and only if $\epsilon(p)=0$. Thus $J$ consists exactly of the fractions $i/s$ with $i\in I$, and in particular $J=IP_S$. This verifies the kernel identification for these specific standard presentations, without any injectivity assumption on $A\to A_S$.

source.place: Tag 07BS (lemma-NL-localize-bottom), the kernel of the localized presentation.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], the map $P\to P_S=T^{-1}P$ is flat. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] to $I\subseteq P$ and using $J=IP_S$ gives the canonical isomorphism $(I/I^2)\otimes_P P_S\xrightarrow{\sim}J/J^2$, $[i]\otimes q\mapsto q[i]$. Put $M=I/I^2$, a $B=P/I$-module. The multiplication map $M\otimes_P P_S\to M$, $m\otimes(p/s)\mapsto\epsilon(p)s_B^{-1}m$, is an isomorphism with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. It is well defined by the fraction relation and tensor bilinearity: multiplication by every $s_B$ is invertible on $M$. For the second inverse identity, the balancing relation gives $s(m\otimes p/s)=(\epsilon(p)m)\otimes1=s((\epsilon(p)s_B^{-1}m)\otimes1)$, and $s$ acts invertibly on the tensor through $P_S$, so it can be cancelled. Therefore the degree $-1$ map $u^{-1}:I/I^2\to J/J^2$, $[i]\mapsto[i/1]$, is a $B$-linear isomorphism, with inverse $[i/s]\mapsto s_B^{-1}[i]$.

source.place: Tag 07BS (lemma-NL-localize-bottom), conormal calculation; Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization); Morphisms Tag 0473 (lemma-conormal-functorial-flat), affine calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] first to $P/A$ and then to $P_S/A_S$, in both cases with variable set $B$. The modules $B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$ and $B\otimes_{P_S}\Omega_{P_S/A_S}$ are free $B$-modules on the respective elements $1\otimes\mathrm dx_b$. The canonical degree $0$ comparison $u^0$ sends each such basis element to the element with the same index. The reverse assignment on these bases is its $B$-linear inverse. Arbitrarily many variables cause no difficulty, since every polynomial and every vector has finite support.

source.place: Tag 07BS (lemma-NL-localize-bottom), differential calculation; Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), applied as the existing arbitrary-variable node.

proof.text: The differential sends $[i]$ to $1\otimes\mathrm di$. The comparison commutes with it: for $i\in I$, both routes give $1\otimes\mathrm d(i/1)$. Indeed, the polynomial differential formula expresses both as $\sum_b\epsilon(\partial i/\partial x_b)(1\otimes\mathrm dx_b)$; the coefficient map fixes the variables and commutes with these formal derivatives. Thus the two isomorphisms just proved are the components of the canonical chain map in the statement. Their inverses form a chain map, since $d_Su^{-1}=u^0d$ implies $d(u^{-1})^{-1}=(u^0)^{-1}d_S$. Both composites are exactly the identities, so the required homotopies are zero. Applying the functor from complexes to $D(B)$ preserves this inverse and proves that the specified map is an isomorphism there. If $0\in S$, existence of $A_S\to B$ forces $B=0$; the same formulas apply to its zero modules.
